sourceScope: Uncommitted tested changes over the base revision. This is not evidence that the base commit already includes the fix.
problem: A terminal failed task whose exact stopped container remained present retained its capacity correctly, but its broad release error aborted each scheduler turn before other projects could use remaining capacity.
correction: Only a positively identified original-engine, immutable owned stopped Docker allocation is classified as item-local cleanup pending. Its lease, resource charge, retained output and failure guidance remain. Other projects may pass their own normal admission gates.

Corrected fixture and original production source fail at the intended starvation assertion: terminal cleanup aborts before three independently admissible projects progress.
The identical four-project test plus new classification cases pass:35 test outcomes,0 failures,0 skips.
Affected API/product race:128 test outcomes,0 failures,0 skips. This includes overlapping tests from the focused run and is not an additional128 unique test claims.

properties: Actual reviewed HTTP queue consent and typed session dispatch with a controlled Docker-shaped backend.
A remains failed with its same stopped immutable container, private settled lease and held-capacity message.
B, C and D each receive exactly one separately owned running child.
Repeated scheduler turns and service/store reopen do not replay or replace any attempt.

negativeCoverage: Running, starting, unknown, missing-ref and mismatched identity/ownership allocations are not local cleanup.
Legacy or unacknowledged launches, changed request, changed engine/instance, unavailable identity/lookup and joined transport ambiguity retain global refusal.
Cancellation, deadline, corrupt shared ledger and joined errors are not converted to local permission.
Classification does not alter private capacity/proof; corrupt shared ledger bytes remain unchanged.
limitations: Controlled Linux Go/API/product/registry mechanics, not actual Docker execution or native Windows testing.
No model-provider quality, sustained-load, UI latency or full-product acceptance claim.
This is a targeted affected race run, not a fresh whole-repository suite.
